conclusions: Accept the C2 screening optimization with the measured parser and resource tradeoffs below. No additional timing supplement is required for this decision.

Incremental screening benefit is attributable to C2 against actual accepted C1b. Cumulative descriptor/conformer gains include previously accepted C1 parallelism and are not attributed to the new cache.

Incremental parsing is consistently slower at all four thread counts, with most wall and CPU pairs slower and both launch orders agreeing. Treat this as a real small regression, not noise; an unchanged parser source does not prove binary-layout causation.

Search wall ratios span large gains and losses and show substantial launch-order effects. No reliable search wall benefit is claimed; negative medians and CPU costs remain reported, including the cumulative search CPU penalties.
Cumulative short-workload and prediction penalties are retained in the complete tables. Several are small absolute durations or noisy, which limits attribution but does not erase their measured cost.

Cumulative descriptor/conformer CPU and RSS increases reflect the accepted parallelism tradeoff. Incremental screening RSS medians shift by less than 0.07 MiB in either direction; this is not evidence of zero memory cost.

All scientific outputs, full gates, inputs, source/binary identities, raw resource records, sample order and postflight receipts were verified by the two independent analyses. Existing scientific-method limitations remain unchanged.

predeclared_target.interpretation: Reproducible targeted benefit across all four settings and both orders, supported by lower paired CPU. Individual pairs are retained, including two wall losses and pairs below 10 percent reduction.
predeclared_target.metric: screen_1000 native wall time versus contemporaneously measured accepted C1b

statistical_policy: Every predeclared measured pair is retained. Warmups are verified and retained separately. Medians, MAD, full ranges and AB/BA effects are descriptive; no confidence-interval or universal improvement claim is introduced.
